key_insight: Positioning a phononic subsurface beneath a separated flat-plate flow can either amplify or attenuate sustained vortex shedding, with one configuration substantially reducing force oscillations.
engineering_relevance: Passive phononic subsurfaces could reduce unsteady aerodynamic loads while largely preserving mean lift and drag.
method: Simulated strongly coupled fluid–structure interaction using a high-fidelity immersed boundary method.
Modeled the subsurface as a grounded diatomic chain driving a compliant plate section.
Varied chordwise position and resonant displacement-amplitude growth; analyzed frequencies, phase relationships, and flow fields.
evidence_signal: Simulations identified four position-dependent limit-cycle regimes and a configuration reducing lift oscillation amplitude by over 30% and drag oscillation amplitude by over 50%, with less than 0.5% change in mean lift and drag.
watch_item: Performance is position-sensitive, and the abstract reports numerical results rather than experimental validation.
paper_title: Interaction of Sustained Vortex Shedding with a Phononic Subsurface: Effect of Positioning and Resonant Characteristics
